content: Within this category, business email compromise and credential theft attacks escalated dramatically, exploiting the decentralized nature of remote workforces and the lack of robust perimeter defenses in home office environments . Conversely, social media platforms accounted for the lowest proportion among the top vectors, comprising exactly 5.0 percent of the attacks. While social media phishing represents a smaller fraction of the overall threat landscape, it remains a critical component of the multi-channel strategies deployed by modern cybercriminals to cast wider nets and bypass traditional security perimeters . The evolution of phishing methods during this timeframe saw attackers diversifying their approaches beyond standard email campaigns. Threat actors increasingly leveraged multi-channel strategies, incorporating SMS-based phishing and malicious QR codes alongside traditional vectors . These diversified tactics were designed to exploit the varied digital habits of different demographic groups. For instance, millennial and Gen-Z demographics have been identified as particularly vulnerable to these multi-channel attacks due to their high levels of digital engagement and constant connectivity . The reliance on mobile devices for both personal and professional tasks created new avenues for attackers to exploit, bypassing legacy enterprise security measures that were primarily designed for on-premises network protection. Furthermore, innovative scams such as calendar invite phishing emerged as novel threats, exploiting trusted productivity applications to deliver malicious links directly to users' daily schedules [35] . While these AI-driven methodologies and novel vectors were only emerging threats during the 2020 to 2023 period, they currently dominate the cybersecurity discourse and represent a formidable challenge for South African enterprises today [35] . Consequently, the South African market exhibits a critical and growing demand for advanced, AI-powered cybersecurity solutions capable of identifying and neutralizing these complex, multi-channel phishing threats in real-time. Addressing the vulnerabilities exposed by the historical reliance on email-based communication, which accounted for 55.0 percent of historical attacks, requires a paradigm shift toward behavioral analytics, continuous authentication, and automated threat remediation tailored to the unique operational realities of the South African digital economy.
